We are looking for a strategic and collaborative executive to lead the Risk Business Management and Governance function. Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Risk Management Transformation and Enablement, you will partner with Risk leaders and enterprise teams to translate priorities into clear plans, provide timely business insights and establish disciplined management routines. Lead Risk Management strategy and annual planning, translating enterprise and Risk priorities into clear objectives, plans and measurable outcomes.
Oversee transformation priorities and investments, supporting prioritization, sequencing, funding decisions and alignment across Risk.
Manage the Risk scorecard, consolidating performance measures, commitments, dependencies and outcomes for executive review.
Provide integrated business insights and recommendations to support strategic trade-offs, resource allocation and timely decision-making.
Lead performance reporting and workforce analytics, providing visibility into capacity, organizational trends and execution against priorities.
Oversee budgeting, forecasting, expense management and financial performance, including variance analysis, cost transparency and investment governance.
Lead business operations and administrative services that enable efficient and consistent execution across the function.
Oversee communications, colleague engagement and workplace requirements in partnership with enterprise teams.
Establish policy frameworks and operating guidance that clarify requirements, ownership and expected practices.
Lead governance disciplines spanning monitoring and testing, issue management, change governance and regulatory programs.
Oversee Business Continuity Management and data governance, including policy and standards, stewardship and data quality.
Create an integrated view of strategy, financials, operations, governance and execution to strengthen organizational discipline and accountability.
Build effective partnerships across Risk and enterprise functions, influencing outcomes through shared accountabilities.
Develop an inclusive, high-performing environment where different perspectives are valued and colleagues are empowered to deliver.

Risk Management leaders and teams across all Risk pillars.
Risk Management Transformation and Enablement leadership.
Enterprise partners across Finance, Human Resources, Technology, Data, Legal, Compliance, Communications, Corporate Real Estate and shared services.

Significant progressive leadership experience in business management, strategy, finance, operations, governance, risk management or enterprise transformation.
Experience leading integrated business planning, executive reporting, scorecards and management routines in a large, complex organization.
Strong financial management experience, including budgeting, forecasting, expense oversight, investment governance and performance analysis.
Experience with workforce analytics, organizational planning, business operations, communications, colleague engagement and workplace coordination.
Strong knowledge of governance disciplines, including monitoring and testing, issue management, change governance, regulatory programs, business continuity, policy frameworks and data stewardship.
Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex information, identify themes and trade-offs, and provide clear recommendations to senior executives.
Strong judgment and the ability to influence, constructively challenge and build alignment across a matrixed organization.
Strong executive communication, organizational awareness and the ability to operate effectively in a highly regulated environment.
Inclusive leadership skills and a commitment to creating an environment where people with different backgrounds and perspectives can contribute and succeed.

jobs.description:
About the Organization

Our client is a family-owned, international food and beverage organization with restaurant operations spanning multiple countries, including Canada. The company operates a growing portfolio of globally recognized quick-service restaurant brands.

With a strong track record of growth and an entrepreneurial culture, the organization continues to invest in its people, operations and finance infrastructure to support its expanding business across multiple entities, brands, jurisdictions and currencies.

About the Opportunity

Our client is seeking a Vice President, Finance to join its senior leadership team and play a critical role in strengthening and evolving the finance function across Canada and the UK.
Reporting to the CFO, this is a broad, highly visible leadership role that combines strategic finance leadership with hands-on ownership of core financial processes. The successful candidate will oversee financial and management reporting, FP&A and commercial finance, treasury and banking relationships, and provide financial leadership on M&A and other strategic initiatives.
The role is well suited to a finance leader who can operate comfortably at both the VP and Controller level - someone who can provide strategic insight and decision support to senior leadership while maintaining a strong grasp of the underlying financial detail and reporting infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Reporting

Take ultimate ownership of the financial and management reporting function across Canada and the UK.
Review and ensure the accuracy, integrity and timeliness of financial reporting prior to presentation to the CFO.
Oversee the preparation and review of monthly, quarterly and annual financial reporting.
Partner with internal and external stakeholders, including auditors and advisors, on financial reporting matters.
Ensure appropriate reporting processes, controls and accounting policies are in place across the organization.
Provide financial insight and analysis to support senior leadership decision-making.

FP&A & Commercial Finance

Lead the annual planning, budgeting and forecasting processes across the business.
Develop and maintain the company's business plan and financial models.
Establish reporting and performance measurement frameworks that connect financial results to business decisions.
Partner with operational and commercial leaders to evaluate performance, identify trends and develop actionable recommendations.
Track performance against budget, forecast and strategic objectives, providing meaningful variance analysis and recommendations.
Support decision modelling and scenario analysis for major business initiatives.
Work closely with the UK finance team, leveraging its established commercial finance and FP&A capabilities while strengthening the Canadian function.

Cash Management & Treasury

Take ownership of cash management and treasury activities across Canada and the UK.
Develop strong relationships with banking partners and financial institutions.
Oversee liquidity, cash flow forecasting and working capital management across two countries and two currencies.
Develop improved visibility and controls around cash movements between Canada and the UK.
Provide senior leadership with clear insight into liquidity, funding requirements and cash flow.

M&A & Strategic Projects

Provide financial leadership and support throughout M&A and other strategic transactions.
Act as a key finance point of contact during transaction execution and subsequent integration.
Partner with the CFO and external advisors on financial analysis, due diligence and transaction-related activities.
Serve as the bridge between transaction execution and the operational transition of acquired businesses.
Lead or participate in other strategic finance initiatives and projects as the business evolves.

Finance Transformation & Systems

Serve as the finance project owner for the company's transition to IFRS 16 lease accounting.
Act as the primary finance point of contact for auditors, consultants and other external advisors throughout the implementation.
Lead the financial requirements and stakeholder coordination associated with the project rather than performing the underlying transactional work.
Support the organization's evolution from its current Sage ERP environment toward Sage Intacct.
Bring experience with ERP implementations, finance transformation and process optimization to help build a more scalable finance infrastructure.

The Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate will be a commercially minded finance leader who combines strong technical accounting and controllership fundamentals with sophisticated FP&A and business partnering capabilities.
You will likely bring:
12+ years of progressive finance experience, with experience operating at a senior finance leadership level.
Experience leading financial reporting and controllership functions in a complex, multi-entity organization.
Strong FP&A, budgeting, forecasting and financial modelling capabilities.
Experience managing cash flow, treasury functions and banking relationships.
Experience working across multiple entities, currencies and/or jurisdictions.
Exposure to M&A, transaction execution and post-transaction integration.
Experience leading finance transformation, ERP implementations or major finance systems projects.
Strong understanding of IFRS and financial reporting requirements.
Experience with IFRS 16 / lease accounting is an asset.
Sage Intacct experience is an asset; broader ERP implementation experience is highly relevant.
Interest in AI as it relates to data analysis and process automation
Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work effectively with executives, operational leaders, auditors, consultants and banking partners.
A hands-on, entrepreneurial approach and the ability to move seamlessly between strategic thinking and detailed execution.
A CPA or equivalent professional accounting designation is preferred.

Food & beverage or restaurant industry experience is not required. The organization is more interested in the complexity, breadth and quality of a candidate's finance leadership experience.

We are passionate about delivering excellent client service, an outstanding Associate experience with opportunities to learn and grow professionally. Sym-Tech is growing quickly and that means endless ways to make a real difference! We are currently recruiting a Director, Finance
to join our headquarters located in Thornhill, ON.

A career with us offers:

A fun, fast paced culture
Opportunities to grow and develop your career
On-going industry training programs and professional development opportunities
A workplace that supports workplace diversity, equity and inclusion
A strong promoter of women in the automotive industry
The chance to work with some of the best in the business!

Position Summary:
Reporting directly to the VP of Finance, the Director, Finance, will play a critical role in strengthening the Company’s core accounting operations, close processes, and financial controls. This role is heavily focused on improving the quality, timeliness, and reliability of financial reporting through process development, simplification, and automation.

The Director, Finance will oversee monthly, quarterly and annual close activities for the consolidated Sym‑Tech entities, ensure strong balance sheet discipline through robust reconciliations and detailed financial reviews, and provide technical accounting guidance across the organization. While the role includes elements of financial analysis and planning, the primary emphasis is on accounting fundamentals, execution excellence, and building scalable, repeatable processes.

The role provides technical accounting guidance throughout the organization to ensure the consistency of accounting practices and principles throughout the operational business.

The successful candidate will be hands‑on, detail‑oriented, and capable of leading teams through change while operating effectively in a growing, complex environment. This position has two direct reports, and overall responsibility for Financial Reporting, OEM Accounting, and select FP&A activities.

Position Functions:

Core Accounting, Close, and Controls

On time, accurate and complete financial reporting for the Company. Analyze and prepare dashboards on balance sheets, income statements, financial position forecasts and capital expenditure reporting.
Manage month‑end, quarter‑end, and year‑end close processes, including journal entries, reconciliations, ad-hoc analyses and financial reporting.
Ensure accurate accounting for bordereaux, premium flows, claims funds, and insurer settlements.
Oversee cash management, trust accounts, and insurer reconciliation processes.
Own and continuously improve the monthly and annual close processes, including developing standardized timelines, checklists, and accountability across the team.
Lead efforts to simplify, automate, and streamline close‑related activities to improve efficiency, accuracy, and cycle time.
Ensure strong balance sheet integrity through timely, well‑documented account reconciliations and resolution of open items.
Perform detailed reviews of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements, with a strong focus on accuracy, completeness, and underlying drivers.
Strengthen core accounting fundamentals, including journal entry discipline, reconciliations, documentation standards, and internal controls.

Financial Reporting & Technical Accounting

Provide timely, insightful financial analysis on divisional and business unit performance, including revenue, margin, expense, and cash drivers.
Champion data-driven culture within the finance team and broader organization.
Oversee all divisional financial reporting, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and alignment with local requirements and US GAAP.
Support the VP, Finance on technical accounting matters, including documentation and assessments for management and external auditors.
Serve as a subject matter expert on accounting standards and their application, including supporting M&A due diligence and integration activities.
Act as the primary liaison with OEM partners for quarterly, interim, and year‑end financial reporting requirements.

Process Improvement & Team Leadership

Develop and implement clear processes, policies, and procedures to support consistent execution across the finance organization.
Lead, coach, and develop the finance team, driving ownership, accountability, and discipline around key deliverables.
Partner with Corporate Finance to ensure alignment on close processes, reporting standards, and reconciliation expectations.

Select Planning & Analysis Support

Provide targeted financial analysis to support management decision‑making, including variance analysis and trend identification.
Support budgeting and forecasting activities as needed, with an emphasis on ensuring inputs are grounded in accurate accounting data.

Audit, Compliance & Governance

Manage relationships with external auditors and oversee audit execution to ensure timely resolution of findings.
Enhance the accuracy and integrity of the Company’s reported financial results.
Ensure compliance with Amynta and Sym‑Tech policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.

Minimum Qualifications & Competencies:
University degree in Business/Accounting, with professional accounting designation (CPA).
5+ years of progressive management experience with knowledge of all aspects of corporate accounting and financial management.
Strong technical accounting skills (i.e. U.S. GAAP) and strong internal controls and procedures.
Strong preference for candidates who have worked in an entrepreneurial, high growth environment in a privately held business.
Demonstrated ability to "roll up the sleeves" and work with the team in a hands-on capacity.
Advanced computer skills (Word, Excel ,and PowerPoint) and knowledge of ERP accounting systems.
Prior exposure to Microsoft NAV and Workday would be an asset.
Ability to hold a strong right hand to general management, with sound judgment on when to appropriately escalate issues and concerns.
Ability to lead a team, driving ownership, accountability, and discipline around key accounting and reporting processes.
Expert in project planning, with a proven ability to organize, prioritize, and manage responsibilities to consistently meet deadlines in environments with overlapping and potentially competing priorities.
Attention to detail and a high degree of accuracy.
Excellent communication and organizational skills with the ability to quickly build credibility, rapport and relationships at multiple levels of the organization
A team player and consensus builder.
Demonstrates strong integrity, social responsibility, and respect, complemented by a flexible, approachable demeanor and a hands-on approach.

Partner with HR, Technology, Finance, and external vendors to align system requirements, manage dependencies, and deliver transformation outcomes.
Ensure compliance with regulatory, audit, and governance requirements related to payroll processing, data integrity, and financial reporting.
Lead cross-functional workstreams and collaborate with program stakeholders to ensure delivery against timelines, scope, and quality expectations.
Support continuous improvement efforts by identifying opportunities to enhance payroll processes, systems, and overall operational efficiency.

jobs.description:
About the Organization

Our client is a family-owned, international food and beverage organization with restaurant operations spanning multiple countries, including Canada. The company operates a growing portfolio of globally recognized quick-service restaurant brands.

With a strong track record of growth and an entrepreneurial culture, the organization continues to invest in its people, operations and finance infrastructure to support its expanding business across multiple entities, brands, jurisdictions and currencies.

About the Opportunity

Our client is seeking a Director, Finance to join its Canadian finance leadership team and play a key role in strengthening the organization's financial reporting and controllership capabilities.

Reporting to the VP, Finance and CFO, this role will have primary responsibility for entity-level and brand-level financial reporting across the Canadian business, with a particular focus on the organization's largest brand portfolio. The Director will also oversee Canadian cash forecasting and provide financial insight and support to senior leadership.

This is a predominantly controllership-focused leadership position, ideally suited to a strong accounting and finance professional who combines technical depth with commercial awareness and the ability to operate in a growing, multi-entity organization.

While the immediate mandate is focused on Canada and core controllership responsibilities, there is meaningful opportunity for the successful candidate to expand their scope over time into group-level FP&A, commercial finance, M&A and broader strategic finance responsibilities.

Key Responsibilities:

Financial Reporting & Controllership

Take ownership of financial reporting across all Canadian legal entities.
Oversee the preparation, review and delivery of accurate and timely monthly, quarterly and annual financial statements.
Ensure appropriate accounting policies, controls and reporting processes are maintained across the Canadian organization.
Review financial results and investigate significant variances, trends and anomalies.
Ensure the integrity and consistency of financial data across entities and reporting periods.
Partner with the VP, Finance and CFO to ensure Canadian reporting meets group requirements.
Coordinate with external auditors, advisors and other stakeholders as required.
Support the ongoing enhancement of financial controls, processes and reporting infrastructure.
Identify opportunities to improve the efficiency, accuracy and scalability of the Canadian finance function.

Brand-Level Reporting

Own financial reporting and analysis across the Canadian brand portfolios.
Develop and maintain brand-level reporting that provides leadership with clear visibility into financial and operating performance.
Analyze brand performance against budget, forecast and prior periods.
Provide meaningful variance analysis and identify key drivers of financial performance.
Partner with operational and brand leadership to translate financial results into actionable business insights.
Ensure consistency between entity-level accounting and brand-level management reporting.

Cash Flow & Treasury

Own cash flow forecasting across the Canadian entities.
Develop and maintain short- and medium-term cash flow forecasts.
Monitor cash requirements, working capital and liquidity across the Canadian business.
Partner with the VP, Finance and CFO on broader treasury and cash management activities.
Provide visibility into upcoming funding requirements and significant cash movements.
Support relationships with banking partners and other financial institutions as required.

FP&A & Commercial Finance

Support the annual budgeting, forecasting and planning processes.
Provide financial analysis and decision support to Canadian leadership.
Partner with operational stakeholders to understand business performance and financial drivers.
Support scenario modelling and analysis for key business initiatives.
Contribute to the development of management reporting and performance metrics.

The precise scope of FP&A and commercial finance responsibilities will evolve as the finance organization continues to develop.

Strategic & Group Finance

Support the VP, Finance and CFO on broader finance initiatives and special projects.
Provide financial analysis and support for strategic initiatives, including potential M&A activity where appropriate.
Participate in finance transformation, systems implementation and process improvement initiatives.
Contribute to initiatives designed to create greater consistency between Canadian and broader group finance processes.
Develop the capability to take on broader group-level responsibilities as the organization and the individual's experience evolve.

The Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate will be a strong controllership and financial reporting leader who is comfortable operating in a dynamic, entrepreneurial environment.

You will likely bring:

8–12+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience, including significant controllership or financial reporting responsibility.
Strong technical accounting and financial reporting capabilities.
Experience overseeing multiple legal entities and/or business units.
Experience producing entity-level and management-level financial reporting.
Strong understanding of budgeting, forecasting and financial analysis.
Experience with cash flow forecasting and working capital management.
Strong analytical skills and the ability to identify the underlying drivers of financial performance.
Experience working with external auditors and other professional advisors.
Experience in a multi-entity, multi-location or complex operating environment.
ERP experience; exposure to Sage or Sage Intacct would be an asset.
Experience with finance transformation or ERP implementation would be considered an asset.
CPA designation or equivalent professional accounting qualification is preferred.
Strong communication skills and the ability to build relationships with senior stakeholders and operational leaders.
A hands-on approach and willingness to operate at both the detailed and strategic levels.
Restaurant or food & beverage industry experience is not required. Experience within a complex, multi-entity organization is more important.

What Makes This Opportunity Unique

This role provides the opportunity to join a growing organization and take meaningful ownership of the Canadian finance and reporting function across multiple entities and brands.

The immediate mandate is strongly rooted in controllership, financial reporting, brand performance and cash forecasting, providing the successful candidate with a broad understanding of the Canadian business.

At the same time, the role has significant room to evolve. As the finance organization grows, there is an opportunity for the Director to expand into FP&A, commercial finance, M&A and broader group-level responsibilities, creating a strong path toward future senior finance leadership opportunities.

Key finance leadership role with direct influence on business growth and strategy.

jobs.title: Vice President, Finance
jobs.description:
The Vice President, Finance, Americas
is responsible for providing strategic financial leadership and oversight across the Americas region. This role partners with executive and business leaders to drive financial performance, support growth initiatives, ensure compliance with financial and regulatory requirements, and deliver accurate financial planning, reporting, and analysis. The VP Finance leads regional finance functions, including accounting, budgeting, forecasting, tax, treasury, internal controls, and financial operations, while fostering a high-performing team and supporting the achievement of organizational objectives.

Reports to the Chief Financial Officer.

Responsibilities

1. Financial Reporting & Accounting

Oversee accounting operations for the Americas region, including general ledger, month-end/quarter-end closing, and consolidation.
Own inventory accounting for the Memphis distribution center — valuation methodology, standard costing, cycle counts, and obsolescence/reserve policy.
Ensure COGS accuracy and margin analysis tied to distribution operations.
Ensure accuracy of financial statements prepared in accordance with local GAAP in each jurisdiction (US, Canada, and LatAm countries).
Prepare and submit financial reports in compliance with IFRS and Group accounting standards, ensuring quality and compliance.
Coordinate with external auditors for annual audits, implement improvement plans, and maintain effective communication with internal and external audit teams.
Work closely with the HQ finance team to ensure consistency in reporting formats, policies, and processes.

2. Compliance

Maintain and enhance internal control and accounting procedures to align with Group policies and US/Canadian/LatAm regulations.
Ensure customs and bonded warehouse compliance — duty deferral, in-bond transfers, and CBP requirements — for the Memphis distribution center, partnering with trade compliance and logistics teams.
Ensure compliance with local direct and indirect tax regulations, including corporate income tax, VAT/GST, and multi-state US sales/use tax nexus; complete filings accurately and on time.
Regularly review the reasonableness of intercompany transfer pricing across US, Canada, and LatAm entities, and assess associated risks.

3. Treasury & Financial Planning

new_jobs.description:
About the Organization

Our client is a family-owned, international food and beverage organization with restaurant operations spanning multiple countries, including Canada. The company operates a growing portfolio of globally recognized quick-service restaurant brands.

With a strong track record of growth and an entrepreneurial culture, the organization continues to invest in its people, operations and finance infrastructure to support its expanding business across multiple entities, brands, jurisdictions and currencies.

About the Opportunity

Our client is seeking a Director, Finance to join its Canadian finance leadership team and play a key role in strengthening the organization's financial reporting and controllership capabilities.

Reporting to the VP, Finance and CFO, this role will have primary responsibility for entity-level and brand-level financial reporting across the Canadian business, with a particular focus on the organization's largest brand portfolio. The Director will also oversee Canadian cash forecasting and provide financial insight and support to senior leadership.

This is a predominantly controllership-focused leadership position, ideally suited to a strong accounting and finance professional who combines technical depth with commercial awareness and the ability to operate in a growing, multi-entity organization.

While the immediate mandate is focused on Canada and core controllership responsibilities, there is meaningful opportunity for the successful candidate to expand their scope over time into group-level FP&A, commercial finance, M&A and broader strategic finance responsibilities.

Key Responsibilities:

Financial Reporting & Controllership

Take ownership of financial reporting across all Canadian legal entities.
Oversee the preparation, review and delivery of accurate and timely monthly, quarterly and annual financial statements.
Ensure appropriate accounting policies, controls and reporting processes are maintained across the Canadian organization.
Review financial results and investigate significant variances, trends and anomalies.
Ensure the integrity and consistency of financial data across entities and reporting periods.
Partner with the VP, Finance and CFO to ensure Canadian reporting meets group requirements.
Coordinate with external auditors, advisors and other stakeholders as required.
Support the ongoing enhancement of financial controls, processes and reporting infrastructure.
Identify opportunities to improve the efficiency, accuracy and scalability of the Canadian finance function.

Brand-Level Reporting

Own financial reporting and analysis across the Canadian brand portfolios.
Develop and maintain brand-level reporting that provides leadership with clear visibility into financial and operating performance.
Analyze brand performance against budget, forecast and prior periods.
Provide meaningful variance analysis and identify key drivers of financial performance.
Partner with operational and brand leadership to translate financial results into actionable business insights.
Ensure consistency between entity-level accounting and brand-level management reporting.

Cash Flow & Treasury

Own cash flow forecasting across the Canadian entities.
Develop and maintain short- and medium-term cash flow forecasts.
Monitor cash requirements, working capital and liquidity across the Canadian business.
Partner with the VP, Finance and CFO on broader treasury and cash management activities.
Provide visibility into upcoming funding requirements and significant cash movements.
Support relationships with banking partners and other financial institutions as required.

FP&A & Commercial Finance

Support the annual budgeting, forecasting and planning processes.
Provide financial analysis and decision support to Canadian leadership.
Partner with operational stakeholders to understand business performance and financial drivers.
Support scenario modelling and analysis for key business initiatives.
Contribute to the development of management reporting and performance metrics.

Strategic & Group Finance

Support the VP, Finance and CFO on broader finance initiatives and special projects.
Provide financial analysis and support for strategic initiatives, including potential M&A activity where appropriate.
Participate in finance transformation, systems implementation and process improvement initiatives.
Contribute to initiatives designed to create greater consistency between Canadian and broader group finance processes.
Develop the capability to take on broader group-level responsibilities as the organization and the individual's experience evolve.

The successful candidate will be a strong controllership and financial reporting leader who is comfortable operating in a dynamic, entrepreneurial environment.

8–12+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience, including significant controllership or financial reporting responsibility.
Strong technical accounting and financial reporting capabilities.
Experience overseeing multiple legal entities and/or business units.
Experience producing entity-level and management-level financial reporting.
Strong understanding of budgeting, forecasting and financial analysis.
Experience with cash flow forecasting and working capital management.
Strong analytical skills and the ability to identify the underlying drivers of financial performance.
Experience working with external auditors and other professional advisors.
Experience in a multi-entity, multi-location or complex operating environment.

This role provides the opportunity to join a growing organization and take meaningful ownership of the Canadian finance and reporting function across multiple entities and brands.

Build financial models for business cases, new markets, and commercial opportunities, with clear visibility into margins and profitability drivers.
Oversee accounting, treasury, and payment operations across multiple currencies and jurisdictions.
Manage liquidity, foreign exchange exposure, settlements, receivables, and other key financial flows.
Ensure compliance with international accounting standards, tax regulations, and statutory requirements.
Coordinate with auditors and external advisors on financial, tax, and regulatory matters.
